instruction_summary: Produce a calibrated 2026 theory update of CDLZ (2019): recalibrate the paper's bunching/labor-demand-elasticity framework on data through 2024, propose the minimal model amendment reconciling the original and $15-era evidence, and validate it.

steps.description: Rebuilt the venv (replication venv was gone): pandas/numpy/scipy/pyfixest 0.60/matplotlib/pyarrow
steps.command: uv venv /workspace/.venv && uv pip install pandas numpy scipy pyfixest matplotlib pyarrow

steps.description: Read paper model section (II.A conceptual framework, own-wage elasticity, Sec IV / Fig V-B Kaitz slope)
Ran the Kaitz-binned employment-effect joint regression 002 was killed on: 5 bins, full sample 1979-2024 (~3 min, foreground)
5-bin paper-era Kaitz function 1979-2016 for side-by-side calibration
Reduced-form slopes (paper Fig V-B object) both eras; calibrate threshold model; validate (paper-era reproduction + W4 episode); write table + figure
Wrote the theory section and reports

key_results.updated_model: e(bite) flat = c0 for bite<=bite*, then e = c0 - s*(bite-bite*): monopsony with a bite-dependent labor-demand elasticity; nests CDLZ at s=0
key_results.statistical_significance: none; the flat model is not rejected, only its central prediction at the frontier

comparison_to_original.note: tilts negative in the extended sample but statistically flat; paper-era reproduces (-0.065)
softened to ~0/negative, concentrated at high-bite frontier cohort
recast as a function of bite eta(b); paper value is the sub-threshold constant
the extended data cross the range the paper flagged as an open question

deviations: Threshold parameters are [CALIBRATED] to moments 001/002 already produced, not from a new in-session structural estimation (per brief item 6, which permits this when structural estimation is infeasible in-session).

No strict temporal hold-out: the high-bite regime is only observed post-2016, so pre-2015 data identify none of the new parameters. Validation is by paper-era reproduction plus post-frontier-episode fit (both options the brief lists).

The model is indexed by BITE, not Kaitz alone: W4 and W5 have near-identical Kaitz (0.513 vs 0.520) but opposite employment effects driven by bite (0.116 vs 0.094). Kaitz is presented as the correlated structural driver for comparability with the paper's frontier language.
Nothing is statistically significant (tightest signal t~-1.7); the update is a central-tendency shift, labeled throughout.
Cross-bin covariance from the joint Kaitz regression was not extracted, so group-level WLS slope SEs treat bins as independent (disjoint events; mild lower bound on SE).
